name: Medistrom Pilot-24 Lite
summary: A 95Wh, 24V CPAP battery that weighs 1.3 lb and stays under the airline 100Wh limit, the pack to carry on flights with a ResMed AirSense 10 or AirMini.
verdict:
The Pilot-24 Lite is the CPAP battery to pack for flights and backpacking trips, provided your machine runs on 24V and you check your real overnight draw first.

**Built for the airline rule.** Medistrom rates it at 95 [watt-hours](/glossary/watt-hours/) from LG lithium-ion cells. That sits under the 100Wh line that the FAA treats as the no-approval limit for carry-on lithium batteries, so you can fly with it, and usually a spare, without asking the airline. It weighs 1.3 lb and measures about 6.7 x 3.5 x 0.8 inches.

**It is a 24V battery.** The DC output is 24V at 3.5A, made for 24V machines such as the ResMed AirSense 10, S9 and AirMini, with optional kits for the DreamStation Go, 3B Luna and Apex iCH. DC straight to the machine means no inverter losses. There is also a 5V/2.5A USB port and an LED flashlight. Buying the wrong voltage is the most common mistake; for 12V machines, look at the dual-voltage [Medistrom Pilot Flex](/gear/medistrom-pilot-flex/).

**Do the runtime math.** Assume about 85Wh usable. At 10W (low pressure, humidifier and heated tube off) that is about 8.5 hours. At 25W it is about 3.4 hours. Turn the humidifier on and it may not last half the night. Our [power station runtime calculator](/tools/power-station-runtime-calculator/) works for this too. Recharge takes 2-3 hours with the AirSense 10 adapter, or 7-9 hours with the AirMini adapter.

Owners love the size and airline status. The main complaint is that one pack rarely covers a full night with humidification. It features in our [best battery backup for CPAP](/best-battery-backup-for-cpap/) guide, where the [EcoFlow River 3 Plus](/gear/ecoflow-river-3-plus/) covers longer home outages.
bestFor: Air travel and backpacking with a 24V CPAP
skipIf: Your CPAP runs on 12V or you need a heated humidifier all night
pros: 24V DC output with no inverter losses
2-3 hour recharge with an AirSense 10 adapter
cons: 24V only, so it does not suit 12V machines
Charger not included; uses your machine's adapter

faqs.q: How long will the Medistrom Pilot-24 Lite run a ResMed AirSense 10?
faqs.a: It depends on pressure and humidification. With about 85Wh usable from the 95Wh pack, a draw of 10W gives roughly 8.5 hours, while 25W gives about 3.4 hours. Turn off the humidifier and heated tube for the longest runtime. With humidification on, plan on a second battery.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Medistrom Pilot-24 Lite and Pilot Flex?
faqs.a: The Pilot-24 Lite is a 95Wh battery with a fixed 24V output for machines like the AirSense 10 and AirMini. The Pilot Flex is a 98Wh battery that switches between 12V and 24V, adds USB-C with 45W output, and weighs 1.2 lb. Choose the Flex if you own a 12V machine.

name: Medistrom Pilot Flex
summary: A 98Wh dual-voltage CPAP battery that powers both 12V and 24V machines, with USB-C charging and a 1.2 lb weight, for travelers who want one pack for any CPAP.
verdict:
The Pilot Flex is the most flexible travel CPAP battery Medistrom makes, because it works with both 12V and 24V machines instead of forcing you to pick the right model.

**One battery, two voltages.** Medistrom rates it at 98 [watt-hours](/glossary/watt-hours/) with dual-voltage output that switches between 12V and 24V. It comes ready for the ResMed AirMini, and adapter cables are listed for the ResMed AirSense 10 and 11, Philips Respironics DreamStation and DreamStation 2, System One 60 Series and React Luna G3. Confirm the cable for your exact machine before you order.

**Airline-friendly and light.** At 98Wh it stays under the 100Wh FAA carry-on limit, so no airline approval is needed. It weighs 1.2 lb and measures about 6.75 x 3 x 0.8 inches, small enough for a CPAP bag. Medistrom lists 500 charge cycles and a 1-year warranty.

**USB-C is the bonus.** It adds a USB-C port rated at 45W in and out, plus an 18W USB-A port. That lets you charge the battery from a laptop charger, or top up a phone or tablet. Recharge takes up to 3 hours from the DC input; the AirMini adapter or USB-C can take up to 6 hours.

**Runtime math.** Assume about 88Wh usable. At 10W that is close to 9 hours; at 25W, about 3.5 hours. Try your numbers in the [power station runtime calculator](/tools/power-station-runtime-calculator/).

Its strengths are USB-C charging and broad compatibility. The main caveat is that most machines need a separate cable kit. Compare it with the 24V-only [Medistrom Pilot-24 Lite](/gear/medistrom-pilot-24-lite/) in our [best battery backup for CPAP](/best-battery-backup-for-cpap/) guide.
bestFor: Travelers with a 12V or 24V CPAP who want one battery
skipIf: You need a full night with a heated humidifier
pros: Cables listed for AirSense 10/11 and DreamStation 1/2
cons: Most machines need a separate cable kit

specs.Recharge Time: Up to 3 hours (up to 6 via AirMini adapter or USB-C)

faqs.q: Does the Medistrom Pilot Flex work with the ResMed AirSense 11?
faqs.a: Yes, with the right cable. Medistrom lists adapter cables for the ResMed AirSense 10 and 11, DreamStation and DreamStation 2, System One 60 Series and React Luna G3. The battery ships ready for the AirMini. Order the cable kit that matches your exact machine.

faqs.q: Can I take the Medistrom Pilot Flex on a plane?
faqs.a: Yes. It is rated at 98Wh, under the FAA's 100Wh limit for carry-on lithium batteries, so no airline approval is needed. Keep it in your carry-on, not checked luggage, and protect the terminals. Medistrom still advises checking with your airline before you fly.

name: Freedom V2 CPAP Battery
summary: A 99.9Wh universal CPAP battery with machine-specific cable kits, just under the airline 100Wh limit, a lower-cost travel option for many CPAP brands.
verdict:
The Freedom V2 is a universal travel battery that squeezes the most capacity allowed under the airline limit, and it works with many machines through cable kits.

**Maximum carry-on capacity.** It is rated at 99.9 [watt-hours](/glossary/watt-hours/), as close to the FAA's 100Wh no-approval line as a battery gets. That is about 5% more than the 95Wh [Medistrom Pilot-24 Lite](/gear/medistrom-pilot-24-lite/). Sellers list 500 charge cycles and a 1-year limited warranty.

**How the voltage works.** The battery itself runs at 12V with up to 8A of output. Machine-specific cable kits connect it to different CPAPs; for 24V machines such as many ResMed models, the cable steps the voltage up. Kits are sold for ResMed S9 and Air10 Series machines, among others. That makes it flexible, but you must buy the correct kit, and the converter adds a small loss on 24V machines.

**Charging.** It accepts 10-28V DC input. Sellers list 2-3 hours at 90W, 3-4 hours at 60W, and 8-9 hours at 20W, so a car outlet or small solar panel can top it up slowly.

**Runtime math.** Assume about 90Wh usable. At 10W, roughly 9 hours; at 25W, about 3.6 hours. A heated humidifier will cut that sharply. Use the [power station runtime calculator](/tools/power-station-runtime-calculator/) with your machine's draw.

Its draw is capacity for the money. The drawbacks are picking the right cable kit and the short warranty. It is an alternative to the picks in our [best battery backup for CPAP](/best-battery-backup-for-cpap/) guide; the [Medistrom Pilot Flex](/gear/medistrom-pilot-flex/) offers native dual-voltage output and USB-C.
bestFor: Flying with a CPAP on a tighter budget
skipIf: You want native 24V output without a converter cable
pros: 99.9Wh, the most allowed without airline approval
Cable kits for many CPAP brands

specs.Features: 99.9Wh, universal cable kits, under airline limit

atAGlance: 99.9Wh, universal cable kits, under airline limit

faqs.q: Does the Freedom V2 battery work with ResMed machines?
faqs.a: Yes, with the right cable kit. The Freedom V2 runs at 12V internally, and machine-specific kits connect it to ResMed S9 and Air10 Series machines and others. For 24V machines, the cable steps the voltage up. Check the kit list for your exact model before ordering.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the Freedom V2 and the Medistrom Pilot-24 Lite?
faqs.a: Both are travel batteries under the 100Wh airline limit. The Freedom V2 holds 99.9Wh at 12V and uses cable kits, including step-up cables for 24V machines. The Pilot-24 Lite holds 95Wh with a native 24V output, a USB port and a 1.3 lb weight. The Medistrom avoids a converter on ResMed machines.

name: Freedom CPAP Battery 160
summary: A 160Wh CPAP battery with 12-24V output and backup power during outages, the bigger option for full nights at home or road trips with airline approval.
verdict:
The Freedom 160 trades the easy airline status of sub-100Wh packs for 60% more capacity, which makes it a better fit for full nights at home and car camping.

**More capacity per night.** It is rated at 160 [watt-hours](/glossary/watt-hours/) with a 12-24V DC output. Assume about 145Wh usable: at 15W that is close to 10 hours, and at 25W about 5.8 hours. That covers a full night for many machines with the humidifier off, where a 95-99Wh pack often falls short. Use the [power station runtime calculator](/tools/power-station-runtime-calculator/) with your machine's actual draw.

**Backup during outages.** Sellers list it as a backup battery, so it can sit between the wall adapter and the CPAP and keep therapy running when the power drops. That is the job a bedside [UPS-style](/glossary/ups-mode/) setup does. It also has a Quick Charge 3.0 USB port and recharges in 2-3 hours, with optional car and solar charging.

**Compatibility.** Sellers list the ResMed AirSense 10, AirSense 11 and AirMini, Philips DreamStation 1 and 2, and React Luna G3, with a separate cable for the Transcend Micro. Confirm the cable for your machine.

**Flying with it.** Between 100 and 160Wh, FAA rules allow lithium batteries in carry-on bags only with airline approval, and you can carry no more than two spares. Some sellers call it FAA compliant; that still means you ask your airline first.

Owners like the full-night capacity. The common complaint is that it is heavier than expected. For easy flying, the [Medistrom Pilot Flex](/gear/medistrom-pilot-flex/) stays under 100Wh; see our [best battery backup for CPAP](/best-battery-backup-for-cpap/) guide.
bestFor: Full nights at home and car camping with a CPAP
skipIf: You fly often and want to skip airline approval
pros: 160Wh covers a full night for many machines
12-24V output for ResMed and Philips machines
Works as backup power during outages

faqs.q: Can I fly with the Freedom CPAP Battery 160?
faqs.a: Usually, with airline approval. FAA rules allow lithium batteries between 100 and 160Wh in carry-on bags only with the airline's approval, and you may carry no more than two spares. Contact your airline before you fly and keep the battery in your carry-on with the terminals protected.

faqs.q: How long will the Freedom 160 run a CPAP overnight?
faqs.a: Often a full night with the humidifier off. With about 145Wh usable from the 160Wh pack, a 15W draw gives close to 10 hours and a 25W draw about 5.8 hours. A heated humidifier and heated tube can double the draw, so turn them off on battery.
